title: 2010 Fox Glacier FU-24 crash

agencies.name: Transport Accident Investigation Commission
agencies.report_title: Report 10-009: Walter Fletcher FU24, ZK-EUF, loss of control on take-off and impact with terrain

summary: A modified Fletcher FU-24 operated by Skydive New Zealand crashed shortly after takeoff on a skydiving flight from Fox Glacier aerodrome. The aircraft's centre of gravity was located beyond its rear limit due to the seating arrangement of unrestrained passengers and weight calculation errors. The aircraft became airborne at too low an airspeed, pitched nose-up until nearly vertical, rolled left, and impacted the ground at a near-vertical angle, killing all 9 occupants.
probable_cause: The aircraft's weight and balance configuration resulted in the centre of gravity being located beyond its rear limit. The aircraft became airborne at too low an airspeed to be controllable, resulting in uncontrollable nose-up pitch. Contributing factors included passengers not individually weighed with estimates used instead, documentation errors not detected by the Civil Aviation Authority, and the aircraft being modified for parachuting without adequate weight and balance controls.

factors.evidence: Centre of gravity at least 0.122m rear of maximum permissible limit created a tendency for nose to pitch up (p. 29)
Each passenger had not been individually weighed, estimates of total weight were used instead, and documentation errors had not been noticed by the CAA (p. 29, 30)
Aircraft was modified for parachuting with no adequate weight and balance controls (p. 29)
Aircraft became airborne early at too low airspeed, pitched upwards until almost vertical, rolled left, and dived toward ground (p. 29, 4)

events.text: Eight passengers from tour group arrived at Fox Glacier aerodrome facilities for tandem skydive jump, divided into 2 groups of 4 (p. 4)
Pilot flew 9 flights in morning totalling 3.6 hours before stopping for 45-minute lunch break; engine shutdown and refueled to 160 litres standard fuel load (p. 4)

Pilot re-boarded aircraft and started engine; each tandem master led passenger to aircraft and boarded; passengers seated on floor in rear of aircraft, tandem masters attached via 4-point harnesses (p. 4)
Last tandem pair loaded and door closed; pilot taxied forward few metres onto runway and increased power to commence takeoff roll, witnessed by about 10 people (p. 4)
Aircraft accelerated normally down airstrip and got airborne at about usual position, possibly earlier than normal (p. 4)
Aircraft continued pitching upward until it appeared almost vertical, reaching extreme pitch-up attitude (p. 4, 29)

At about 100 metres altitude aircraft entered wing-over to the left to point almost vertically downwards; some witnesses recounted aircraft appeared to maneuver out of dive before left wing lowered further (p. 4)

Aircraft struck ground in near-vertical attitude 100 metres south of runway about 200 metres past end of bitumen section; fine mist or vapour shrouded aircraft on impact then erupted into flames; emergency services notified at 13:27 (p. 4, 5)

recommendations.text: Alert all pilots and operators using Fletcher FU24-954 aircraft for parachuting operations that when loaded with 6 or more passengers it is possible for the aircraft CG to be aft of allowable limit, that this could result in control difficulties, and that parachutists should be seated in forward cabin area, preferably restrained to prevent moving rearward
recommendations.outcome: Emergency Airworthiness Directive DCA/FU24/179 issued 11 September 2010 restricting maximum occupancy and requiring weight and balance calculations for each flight

recommendations.text: As a matter of urgency review the approvals granted for the FU24-954 aircraft with view to amending Flight Manual to allow more accurate determinations of aircraft centre of gravity, and extend review to other conversions of Fletcher and Cresco aircraft
recommendations.outcome: Emergency Airworthiness Directive DCA/FU24/180 issued to address CG limit issues in parachute configurations and review all AFM parachute operation supplements

recommendations.text: Ensure that high engineering standards are maintained by the aircraft maintenance organisations that performed ZK-EUF modification and other similar organisations
recommendations.outcome: Newly introduced risk-based surveillance processes improved effectiveness of CAA audits through better targeting and focus on risk issues

recommendations.text: Take necessary action to ensure thorough and coordinated oversight when accepting aircraft modifications and approving changes in category, especially for specialised operations like parachuting
recommendations.outcome: CAA amended conditions of all design delegation holders effective 24 August 2010 to enable closer oversight of major design changes

recommendations.text: Monitor outcome of joint FAA/USPA study on seat restraints and determine if any findings are applicable for New Zealand parachuting industry
recommendations.outcome: Director committed to monitor the study and consider applicability to New Zealand aviation environment

recommendations.text: Ensure coordinated and proactive approach by relevant departments within CAA to ensure safety efforts are best directed to promote coordinated safe management of flying activities
recommendations.outcome: CAA undergoing major change programme to target resources more effectively; Civil Aviation Rule Part 115 enables closer oversight of commercial parachute operations

recommendations.text: Promote introduction of drug and alcohol detection and deterrence regime for persons employed in safety critical transport roles
recommendations.outcome: Ministry monitoring international experience; Civil Aviation Rule Part 115 provides incentive through safety certification risks

safety_changes: Emergency Airworthiness Directive DCA/FU24/179 restricting maximum occupancy and requiring weight and balance calculations for parachuting operations
Emergency Airworthiness Directive DCA/FU24/180 addressing CG limit issues and reviewing all AFM parachute operation supplements
Civil Aviation Rule Part 115 requiring tandem parachute operators to be certificated with CAA oversight
CAA design delegation holder amendments effective 24 August 2010 enabling closer oversight of major design changes
